meta.title: What's real vs mocked: Cybercrime Report & Tracking
meta.description: An honest, specific account of what this prototype actually does, what is simulated, and what we deliberately did not build.

title: What's real, and what's mocked
intro: This is a hackathon prototype, not an official government service. It does not have, does not claim, and cannot claim government-grade security. It demonstrates the UX and architecture shape of what a production system would require, with mock and synthetic data only. It performs no real authentication, sends no real SMS, holds no real citizen data, and connects to no government system.
heroImageAlt: A person writing notes by hand in a notebook.
keyFactTitle: The single most important fact on this page
keyFactBody: Complaint IDs generated by this prototype are not real NCRP complaint numbers. They are not registered with cybercrime.gov.in, the National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal, CFCFRMS, or any police system. If you have actually been a victim of cybercrime, please use the real portal at cybercrime.gov.in or call 1930.
featureByFeatureIntro: Every control in this product falls into one of four states. Nothing is left ambiguous.

otp.label: OTP / mobile verification
otp.body: No real SMS gateway exists anywhere in this product. In the report and track flows a fresh code is generated per request and shown on screen, there is no fixed fallback that always works. The simulated Aadhaar sign-in is the single exception: it uses a fixed code, on purpose, so a live demo is repeatable, and that code is printed on the screen that asks for it. The ordering, capturing the report first and verifying identity afterwards, is the real design decision; the gateway behind it is simulated.

aadhaarSignIn.label: Aadhaar sign-in
aadhaarSignIn.body: The optional sign-in accepts Aadhaar-shaped numbers that this prototype invented and keeps in its own database. Nothing is sent to UIDAI or any government system, and no check against any real service happens at any point. Only numbers beginning 0000 are accepted, UIDAI never issues a number starting with 0, so a real Aadhaar number is rejected before it is looked up, logged or stored. The code is always 123456 and is shown on the screen that asks for it. No Aadhaar number is ever attached to a complaint, and you never need to sign in to report anything.

sessions.label: Sessions
sessions.body: Session cookies and server-side session records are implemented the way a production system would build them (HTTP-only, short expiry, explicit logout), even though the credential that creates them is a mocked OTP.

passwords.label: Passwords
passwords.body: There is no password anywhere in this product. Nothing to leak, nothing to hash badly.

scanning.label: Evidence "scanning"
scanning.body: Any file you attach is marked with a simulated clean-scan status. No antivirus or malware scanning actually runs on uploaded files.

encryption.label: Encryption at rest
encryption.body: The prototype database has no field-level encryption, no key management, and no access-control layer. A production system handling real complaint narratives, contact details and evidence would need all of these. They are designed for, in the data model, but not implemented here.

notifications.label: Notifications (SMS / email)
notifications.body: Status-update messages are rendered on screen exactly as they would be sent. Nothing is actually delivered to any phone or inbox.

bankFreeze.label: Bank freeze / CFCFRMS coordination
bankFreeze.body: Nothing you submit here is sent to any bank, to CFCFRMS, or to any nodal freeze system. The report is stored in this prototype's own database only.

govConnection.label: Connection to any real government system
govConnection.body: This prototype is not connected to cybercrime.gov.in, NCRP, CFCFRMS, or any other government system, in any direction. It is prohibited by the hackathon's own rules, and we would not have built it that way regardless.

whyNotTitle: Why Aadhaar, PAN, and DigiLocker are not here
whyNotIntro: This is a deliberate product decision, not an oversight, and not something we ran out of time for. We evaluated each one against a single question: does it help freeze the money, route the case, or contact the victim faster? If the answer was no, it does not belong in the product.

aadhaar.title: Aadhaar: never in the reporting flow; simulated in the optional sign-in
aadhaar.body: Using real Aadhaar numbers is explicitly on this hackathon's prohibited list. Beyond that rule, a hackathon team has no lawful basis to authenticate against Aadhaar at all: UIDAI's own onboarding form requires a declared statutory basis (a government subsidy, benefit or service, or another Act of Parliament) that a prototype simply doesn't have, and the private-entity authentication route that once existed under Section 57 of the Aadhaar Act was removed by law in 2019, specifically to stop private parties from doing this. So the reporting flow never asks for an Aadhaar number, and none is ever stored against a complaint, that is the part that matters, and it has not changed. What this build does have is an optional demo sign-in that borrows the Aadhaar-number shape to show a returning citizen being recognised rather than made to register again. It accepts only invented 0000-prefixed numbers, which UIDAI never issues, so it cannot accept anyone's real number and it authenticates against nothing but this prototype's own table of fake records.

pan.title: PAN: never asked, never stored
pan.body: PAN doesn't help freeze the money (that depends on the beneficiary account or UPI ID, not the victim's tax identity), doesn't help route the complaint (routing is by the complainant's State and District), and doesn't help reach the victim (that's the mobile number). It is a permanent, sensitive financial identifier with no functional benefit here, so there is no column for it anywhere in this product's database.

digilocker.title: DigiLocker: designed, deliberately mocked, kept out of this build
digilocker.body: DigiLocker is genuinely the best-shaped identity idea of the three: it's consent-based, it fetches a document rather than collecting a number, and the citizen holds the credential rather than us. But real onboarding requires an incorporated entity with regulatory authorisation to authenticate the relevant document class, which this prototype does not have. More decisively: there is no DigiLocker test sandbox. The official onboarding SOP says plainly that no requests for temporary test access will be entertained. There was no honest way to demonstrate a working DigiLocker call in this build, so it isn't here, not even as a labelled mock button. If it is ever built, it must be optional, consent-first, permanently labelled "Simulated, not connected to DigiLocker", and skippable in one tap.

identitySummary: What we built instead: a small profile, name (optional), mobile number, and State + District, created only after you file a report, never as a gate before it. That is the entire identity system in this product.
noBugs: Known bugs: none, at time of writing.

digilocker.body: No sandbox exists and the official process refuses temporary test access. Any DigiLocker element in this product is a labelled design mock or it does not exist.

aadhaar.strong: Real Aadhaar authentication is excluded by both law and the hackathon's own rules.
aadhaar.body: This is not a design preference. The optional sign-in only ever handles invented 0000-prefixed numbers that no real Aadhaar number can match.

dpdp.strong: India's DPDP data-protection rules are not yet legally binding.
dpdp.body: The substantive obligations (notice, consent, security safeguards, breach notification, erasure) come into force on 13 May 2027; a consent-manager rule follows on 13 Nov 2026. We build to that standard now, as forward-compliance, but we do not and cannot claim to be "DPDP compliant" today, because most of the law isn't in force yet. See <link>/privacy</link>.

tests.body: A deliberate three-day tradeoff, stated openly rather than hidden.

security.strong: The prototype has no production security and cannot claim any.
security.body: Mocked OTP, simulated virus scanning, no encryption at rest, no real access control.

unsolved.strong: Three problems stay named and unsolved:
unsolved.body: getting complaints converted into FIRs, the quality of police follow-up after a complaint is filed, and 1930's call capacity and language routing. A better web form doesn't fix any of these, and we are not pretending it does.
